_comment: THE BACKLINK LIST. Every place that could link to the Green Fire site, why it would, and how to get it. Status is idea, asked, live or lost. Only `live` and `lost` need `at`: the page that holds (or held) the link. `node _TOOLS/operator/seo.mjs links` fetches each `at` page and checks the link is really there and whether it is nofollow, so a link is never counted because someone said it exists. Rows marked `verify: true` came from research, not from a page anyone has opened; check the outlet still takes submissions before spending time on it. Ranked by `tier`: 1 is yours to place today, 2 comes from work you already do, 3 is earned outreach.
rules: One real link from a relevant site beats fifty directory listings. Never buy links, never join link swaps or private blog networks: Google treats them as spam and the penalty lands on this domain.
Every client build and every 3D map ships with a small 'Built by Green Fire' credit link, agreed in the scope, not added quietly.
Pitch the story, not the link. Editors link to people with something only they can say: a working AI setup run by a touring musician is that.
No em dashes in any pitch. It is the tell that a machine wrote it.

targets.why: Your own artist site, already indexed with its own audience. A footer or bio line linking 'AI workshops and dashboards' to /start passes real authority and tells Google the two are the same person.
targets.how: Add one line to the GMS site footer and the bio page: 'I also teach AI and build AI dashboards at Green Fire' linking to /start. GMS stays separate; this is a link, not a merge.

targets.why: The org profile and every public repo have a website field. These links are nofollow, but they are crawled, they help AI answers connect the projects to the site, and developers click them.
targets.how: Set the website field on the org and on each public repo to the site, and add a profile README that links to /open-source and /blog/.

targets.why: Nofollow, so little ranking value, but they are where people who already know you look first, and they confirm the brand to Google's entity graph.
targets.how: Put the /start link in each Green Fire bio. The GMS bios keep their own link.

targets.why: The single strongest local signal for 'AI workshop Austin' style searches. A service area business needs no public street address.
targets.how: Create a profile as a service area business around Austin, category 'Business management consultant' or 'Educational consultant', link to /start. Needs Jordan: Google verifies by phone or video.

targets.why: Bing feeds ChatGPT search and Copilot. Importing from Google Business takes minutes once that exists.
targets.how: Import the Google Business Profile into Bing Places after it is verified.

targets.why: The link that scales with the business. A small credit on a land project or festival site is relevant, editorial and permanent.
targets.how: Add one line to the build scope in startOffers.json and the /tech inquiry reply: a 'Built by Green Fire' credit linking to /tech or /start, with the client's agreement.

targets.site: Festivals and eco villages you play or build for
targets.why: Festivals list artists and partners with links. A performer page that links to your artist site and a partner page that links to Green Fire are both normal and relevant.
targets.how: When a show is confirmed, ask the promoter to link the artist bio to the GMS site and, where Green Fire did media, 3D or AI work, list Green Fire as a partner.

targets.why: Each workshop date is a real event that calendars publish with a link. They bring sign ups as well as links.
targets.how: List each AI workshop date with a link to /start. Austin calendars to check: Do512 and the Austin Chronicle events calendar.

targets.site: Awesome lists and open source directories
targets.why: BioRegional OS is genuinely open source and genuinely unusual. Curated lists on GitHub for sustainability, civic tech and commons software link to repos and project sites.
targets.how: Once the BioRegional OS repo is public with a README, open a pull request to two or three relevant curated lists. One project per list, written plainly.

targets.site: Qwoted, Featured, Help a B2B Writer
targets.why: Writers ask for expert quotes on AI for small business and for musicians. A quote with your name and site in a trade article is one of the most valuable links a small site can get.
targets.how: Make a free profile on one of them, set alerts for AI, small business and independent music, and answer two a week with something only you could say.

targets.why: 'How I run my music business with AI' is exactly what independent artist publications cover. A link from one is relevant and sends readers who are your workshop audience.
targets.how: Offer the music business post as an exclusive, rewritten for them, to one publication at a time. Check each one's contributor guidelines first.

targets.site: Creator, music business and small business podcasts
targets.why: Show notes link to the guest's site, and a conversation about a musician who automated his whole business is an easy yes for hosts.
targets.how: Pitch three shows a month with a one paragraph story and one specific thing listeners will learn.

targets.site: Austin local news and business press
targets.why: A local story links to the site and is the strongest signal for local searches.
targets.how: Pitch the local angle: an Austin musician teaching local businesses to run on AI, tied to a workshop date.

targets.site: A free tool or template on the blog
targets.why: People link to free, useful things far more than to services. A free AI booking letter template or a 'what to automate first' checklist earns links on its own.
targets.how: Publish one free asset as a blog post, then mention it in every pitch above.
